messages:
sophie (cs): Customers calling /v1/generate hitting 503s since ~09:40 UTC, multiple tenants.
sophie (cs): Error seen in gateway: "upstream worker error: exit status 137 / signal 9" and some segfault traces.
sophie (cs): Raising as high priority — support is fielding angry customers (billing/SLAs).
raj (eng-runtime): looking. any node ids or model names?
sophie (cs): customer reports model=redwood-v2-large, route=hosted-west-1, node saw: gpu-134. attaching logs below.
liam (eng-ml): could be kv-prefetch/memory surge on long contexts + large batch. did they change batch_size or context length?
nora (support): customer payloads show context len ~120k tokens (they do long document summaries) and they recently increased parallel requests.
emma (oncall): adding emergency paging, @raj can you check OOM/sigsegv on gpu-134 and whether container restarted?
raj (eng-runtime): container restart happened at 09:41:12. GPU OOM metric spiked to 98% and cgroup killed process. logs excerpt: ```
[09:41:11.823] runtime: fatal error: memory exhausted
[09:41:11.824] infer-runner[pid=2345]: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[09:41:12.001] kernel: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f2a3d...
[09:41:12.120] orchestrator: container exited code=137
```
raj (eng-runtime): also saw KV cache prefetch spike and sustained allocator failures.
liam (eng-ml): model uses large KV cache for 120k context; with multiple parallel requests and high batch_size, memory oversubscription is likely.
alex (sales): one enterprise customer is on phone, wants ETA and workaround. billing concerns flagged.
nora (support): workaround suggested: reduce batch_size to 1 and cap context length to 32k tokens for now. customer can't do that immediately; can we route them to dedicated infra?
emma (oncall): typo above: @emma. We can temporarily fallback their requests to dedicated pool if they have entitlement. if not, we can route to a smaller model variant (redwood-v2-medium) until fix.
raj (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: enable eviction backpressure on hosted-west-1, reduce default per-tenant batch gating, and hotfix to crash handler to avoid full node crash (kill runner earlier, let orchestrator recycle).
emma (oncall): who's taking the hotfix? @raj?
raj (eng-runtime): I'll ship a config tweak to limit prefetch parallelism and clamp batch merges in the serving runtime. prepping a canary.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: runtime-config-v2026.03.17-rc1 -> hosted-west-1-canary
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-17-4412345600. Paging oncall.
liam (eng-ml): also recommend adding an eval check: run long-context stress test on v2-large at QPS=10 with parallelism=8 to reproduce. I have a repro script.
liam (eng-ml): repro steps: ```
# stress repro (internal)
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  curl -X POST https://hosted-west-1/api/v1/generate -d @long_context.json &
done
```
liam (eng-ml): long_context.json uses 100k tokens padded + batch_size=4
raj (eng-runtime): good. @emma please coordinate with support to throttle the customer's traffic and inform them of temporary routing options.
emma (oncall): will notify customer and apply temporary throttle (50% of previous QPS).
raj (eng-runtime): will push config canary now, monitor GPU memory, and abort if we see >90% sustained.
deploy-bot: canary started at 09:48 UTC.
raj (eng-runtime): canary looks stable on two nodes after 5 minutes; memory spike amplitude reduced. rolling to additional hosts.
alex (sales): please send a short note to the customer about mitigation and ETA; they'll want billing credit discussed.
nora (support): sending note now and offering 10% credit while we investigate.
sophie (cs): thanks team — once root cause confirmed (prefetch + oversized batches on long contexts), let's add a docs blurb and a default safety cap for long-context routes.
liam (eng-ml): long-term fixes: smarter prefetch throttling, dynamic kv eviction, and fallbacks to quantized variants under memory pressure.
raj (eng-runtime): opening follow-up PRs: #4578 limit-prefetch-parallelism, #4579 backpressure-thresholds, will link to postmortem.
emma (oncall): incident transitioning to triage. timeline: 09:40 customer reports -> 09:41 node crash -> 09:48 config canary -> 09:55 rollout -> 10:05 throttles + customer notified.
sophie (cs): closing loop: I'll schedule a customer follow-up call for 14:00 UTC.
